graph_edits.rationale: Broaden the carved ground response so the access edge reads as a usable public void rather than a minor nick.
Increase the depth of the cave to strengthen threshold publicness and section legibility at the frontage.
Open the split more clearly so the public threshold becomes visible in elevation and plan without breaking the dominant mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent stepped bar across all views, with a clear dominant mass and acceptable hierarchy. It is not visually over-fragmented and the repair appears clean. The stepped silhouette is legible and capacity-bearing enough for an early neighborhood-living mass, but the public void / ground threshold is weak: the blue access edge is acknowledged only indirectly, with no strong carved court or entry seam. Sectionally it remains mostly a stacked object with limited evidence of a truly active ground/public interior relation, so it passes program fit but only moderately. The best precedent match is the stepped/courtyard logic of the similar references, while the counterfactual terrace-ribbon reference suggests a transferable move toward a more continuous carved public section if further development is needed.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact stepped mass can work for neighborhood-scale public/commercial occupation if the ground edge stays active.
